metadata.title: Why the Same Number Can Be Three Different Claims
metadata.topic: COMMUNICATING UNCERTAINTY · CALIBRATING CLAIMS TO EVIDENCE
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: how the exact same 87% accuracy metric can be written as observe, find, or conclude — and why only one is telling the truth. Lands the carry-out that every claim-verb has an evidence price.
metadata.anchor_pair: B08 -> B09 (sentence dial climbing 8-rung ladder as evidence stacks beneath it)
metadata.one_flag: B10 — editorial standard vs physical law

beats.narration_text: When a model hits eighty-seven percent on a benchmark, does that score tell you what you can conclude? It doesn't. The number is data. The verb is a claim with an evidence price.

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types naive question, hesitates on 'what we can conclude?', corrects to 'what verb we've earned?'

props.text:
If a model hits 87% accuracy,
does the score tell us
what we can conclude?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per course-skepticism SKILL.md. Liam reads over typing animation.

beats.narration_text: Three engineers inspect the exact same model run. The held-out test score is eighty-seven percent. Engineer A writes 'we observe.' Engineer B writes 'we find.' Engineer C writes 'we conclude.' Only one of them is telling the truth.

shot.new_visual_element: Benchmark card 87% accuracy with three diverging engineering write-ups

production_viz.label: Three Engineers, One Score
production_viz.mechanic: Fixed 87% benchmark result card with three competing verb write-ups below it.

beats.narration_text: Eighty-seven percent looks like a hard, objective fact. But in a validation report, the verb does the heavy lifting. Changing that one word transforms a local measurement into a sweeping guarantee, without altering a single digit of data.

shot.new_visual_element: The Verb Inflation Gauge: local observation versus sweeping guarantee

production_viz.label: The Invisible Inflation
production_viz.mechanic: Constant 87% data line against an escalating claim-strength gauge.

beats.narration_text: The natural assumption is that claim strength scales with the score: seventy percent suggests, eighty-seven percent finds, and ninety-nine percent concludes. But accuracy is an outcome, not an evidentiary warrant.

shot.new_visual_element: Score-to-verb mapping assumption struck through with terracotta slash

production_viz.label: Wrong Guess: Score Dictates the Verb
production_viz.mechanic: Linear score-to-verb mapping struck through; accuracy shown as outcome not warrant.

beats.narration_text: Claims operate on warranted assertibility: you are entitled to assert only what your evidence pays for. The discipline uses a frozen eight-rung ladder: hypothesize, suggest, observe, find, show, demonstrate, conclude, prove.

shot.new_visual_element: Warranted assertibility hierarchy: The frozen eight-rung ladder

production_viz.label: Warranted Assertibility & The Frozen Ladder
production_viz.mechanic: Eight-rung vertical ladder of verbs with price tags.

beats.narration_text: The entry rungs cost little. 'Hypothesize' requires only a reason to explore. 'Suggest' requires data consistent with an idea without ruling out rivals. 'Observe' requires a clean measurement with its conditions stated.

shot.new_visual_element: Entry rungs illuminated: Hypothesize, Suggest, Observe

production_viz.label: The Entry Rungs
production_viz.mechanic: Detailed cards showing required receipts for Hypothesize, Suggest, and Observe.

beats.narration_text: 'Find' costs replication: the result must hold across seeds or parameter variations. 'Show' costs robustness and actively ruling out alternative explanations. A single run can never buy 'show,' no matter how high the score.

shot.new_visual_element: Mid rungs illuminated: Find and Show with replication and robustness checks

production_viz.label: The Mid Rungs: Find and Show
production_viz.mechanic: Evidence requirements: multi-seed replication for Find, alternative ruling-out for Show.

beats.narration_text: 'Demonstrate' requires a purpose-built stress experiment with formal controls. 'Conclude' means the motivating question is settled and survives sensitivity checks. And 'prove' is reserved strictly for formal mathematics.

shot.new_visual_element: Top rungs illuminated: Demonstrate, Conclude, Prove

production_viz.label: The Summit: Demonstrate, Conclude, Prove
production_viz.mechanic: Rigorous evidentiary gates for the summit verbs.

beats.narration_text: Watch the sentence on screen. The verb slot is a dial. As we stack evidence beneath it—first a single run, then replicated seeds, then subgroup audits, then adversarial stress tests—the dial climbs from observe to find, show, and conclude.

shot.new_visual_element: MANIM MOVE accumulate: Evidence blocks stack beneath sentence as verb dial climbs

production_viz.label: Accumulate: Stacking Evidence Beneath the Dial
production_viz.mechanic: Sentence template with animated verb dial stepping upward as evidence blocks accumulate.

beats.narration_text: Now look back at our three engineers. They had one run on one held-out split. That evidence pays the price for 'observe.' Engineer B borrowed unbacked credit. Engineer C committed outright verb inflation.

shot.new_visual_element: Auditing the three engineers: Engineer A paid in full, B unbacked, C inflated

production_viz.label: Anchor Payoff: Auditing the Three Claims
production_viz.mechanic: Evaluating the three write-ups against the single-run receipt.

beats.narration_text: One flag — this eight-rung hierarchy is an editorial standard for calibration, not a law of physics. Different teams may use slightly different terms, but the core principle is universal: every verb requires evidentiary receipts.

shot.new_visual_element: One flag card: Editorial calibration standard vs universal law

production_viz.label: One Flag: Operational Standard vs Universal Law
production_viz.mechanic: Flag card showing agreed operational standard demanding evidence receipts.

beats.narration_text: In one direction, a ninety-nine percent score on a single benchmark does not buy you 'conclude.' Without replication, distribution shifts, and sensitivity analysis, you have only paid for 'observe.'

shot.new_visual_element: Direction A card: 99% accuracy on single run is still capped at 'observe'

production_viz.label: Direction A: High Accuracy Capped at Observe
production_viz.mechanic: High single-run metric blocked at rung 3 without replication receipts.

beats.narration_text: In the other direction, writing 'observe' or 'find' does not diminish your engineering. Modest, calibrated verbs survive peer scrutiny, while inflated claims collapse the moment someone checks your test setup.

shot.new_visual_element: Direction B card: Calibrated verbs survive scrutiny; inflated claims collapse

production_viz.label: Direction B: Calibrated Verbs Protect Engineering
production_viz.mechanic: Honest claims standing resilient against audit versus collapsed inflated claims.

beats.narration_text: Every claim-verb has an evidence price — you can only spend the verb your validation actually paid for.

props.quote: Every claim-verb has an evidence price — you can only spend the verb your validation actually paid for.

beats.note: BCRY is the single carry-out sentence, serif, large.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Take the last validation report or model card your team drafted. Highlight every occurrence of observe, find, show, and conclude. For each one, list the exact evidence backing that sentence: was it a single run, replicated seeds, subgroup checks, or a stress test? If the evidence doesn't pay the verb's price, downgrade it to the rung it earned. Liam, in for Bear.
